'''Joshua Michael Richardson''' (born September 15, 1993)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Josh Richardson – Prospect Analysis |url=http://www.nba.com/draft/2015/prospects/josh_richardson |access-date=June 25, 2015 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player, who played ten seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]], earning first-team all-conference honors in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) as a senior in 2015. He was selected in the second round of the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]] and spent the majority of his career there, but has also played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[San Antonio Spurs]], and [[New Orleans Pelicans]].

==High school career==
Richardson averaged 16.5 points, 6.2 rebounds and 3.6 assists as a point guard in his senior year at [[Santa Fe High School (Edmond, Oklahoma)|Santa Fe High School]] in [[Edmond, Oklahoma]]. That year, he was named to the Oklahoma Coaches Association "Large West" All-State Team and ''[[The Oklahoman]]'''s Super 5 first team.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web |title=Josh Richardson Bio |url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/josh_richardson_756929.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170130014803/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/josh_richardson_756929.html |archive-date=January 30, 2017 |access-date=June 25, 2015 |publisher=[[University of Tennessee]]}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Josh Richardson at the line.jpg|thumb|right|Richardson at the free throw line for the Volunteers]]
Richardson played all four seasons at [[University of Tennessee]], appearing in 136 career games for the [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Volunteers]] and averaged 9.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.08 steals and 28.2 minutes while shooting 45.6 percent from the field, 31.8 percent from three-point range and 75.8 percent from the foul line. He finished his career ranking third in school history in games played, ninth in minutes (3,802), ninth in starts, 10th in steals (147), 16th in blocks (88) and 28th in points (1,252).<ref name="2015Draft">{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2015 |title=HEAT Select Justise Winslow |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-select-justise-winslow |access-date=June 26, 2015 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref>

As a junior with the Volunteers, he averaged 10.3 points and 2.8 rebounds per game. In his senior season, Richardson averaged 16.0 points and 4.5 rebounds per game and was named to the First Team All SEC, the SEC All-Defensive Team and the Defensive All-American Team.<ref name="Bio" /><ref name="2015Draft" />

==Professional career==
===Miami Heat (2015–2019)===
On June 25, 2015, Richardson was selected with the 40th pick of the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]].<ref name="2015Draft" /> On August 3, 2015, he signed with the Heat after averaging 11.8 points and 2.8 rebounds in 10 summer league games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2015 |title=HEAT Signs Josh Richardson |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-josh-richardson |access-date=August 3, 2015 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> He failed to appear in the Heat's first four games of the season before making his NBA debut on November 5 against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], playing in just under seven minutes of action.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Josh Richardson 2015–16 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/richajo01/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=November 13, 2015 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> On November 12, in just his third NBA game, Richardson started at shooting guard in place of the absent [[Dwyane Wade]]. He subsequently recorded eight points and three rebounds in 20 minutes of action, as the Heat defeated the [[Utah Jazz]] 92–91.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 12, 2015 |title=Bosh scores 25, Johnson adds 17 and Heat top Jazz 92–91 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151112/UTAMIA/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead Basketball Association}}</ref> On December 30, he was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]], the Heat's [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2015 the NBA, scoring 15 points on 5-of-6 shooting off the bench in a 118–111 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2016 |title=Curry, Thompson come through late, Bulls 118–96 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/MIACHI/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170108011007/http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/MIACHI/gameinfo.html 2016 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref>[[File:Erik Spoelstra, Josh Richardson (31010132661).jpg|thumb|Richardson listening to Heat head coach [[Erik Spoelstra]] during a game in 2016]]
In July 2016, Richardson re-joined the Heat for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]. On September 9, 2016, he sustained a partially torn [[medial collateral ligament]] in his right knee,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |date=September 9, 2016 |title=Sources: Heat guard Josh Richardson has partially torn MCL |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources-heat-guard-josh-richardson-has-partially-torn-mcl-214956456.html |access-date=September 9, 2016 |publisher=Yahoo!}}</ref> that sidelined him for six to eight weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2016 |title=Josh Richardson says he has been told he will... |url=https://twitter.com/IraHeatBeat/status/774658716893413376 |access-date=September 11, 2016 |via=Twitter}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=November 2020}} On December 27, 2016, he tied a career high with 22 points in a 106–94 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2016 |title=Westbrook gets 15th triple-double, Thunder top Heat 106–94 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899915 |access-date=December 27, 2016 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

On September 18, 2017, Richardson signed a four-year, $42 million contract extension with the Heat.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 18, 2017 |title=HEAT Signs Josh Richardson to Contract Extension |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-josh-richardson-extension |access-date=September 18, 2017 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cato |first=Tim |date=September 13, 2017 |title=Josh Richardson, Heat agree to a 4-year, $42 million contract, per report |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2017/9/13/16304940/josh-richardson-heat-nba-free-agency-deal-signs-extension-contract |access-date=September 18, 2017 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref> On December 1, 2017, he scored a career-high 27 points in a 105–100 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2017 |title=Richardson's career night lifts Heat past Hornets, 105–100 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975072 |access-date=December 2, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On December 16, 2017, he set a new career high with 28 points in a 90–85 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2017 |title=Richardson scores 28 points, Heat beat Clippers 90–85 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975183 |access-date=December 17, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On February 7, 2018, he had a 30-point effort in a 109–101 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 7, 2018 |title=James Harden scores 41 points, Rockets beat Heat 109–101 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975552 |access-date=February 7, 2018 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

On October 29, he scored a career-high 31 points in a 123–113 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2018 |title=Kings run away after halftime, top Heat 123–113 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070770 |access-date=October 29, 2018 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On November 3, he set a new career high with 32 points in a 123–118 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2018 |title=Trae Young scores 24 as Hawks beat Heat 123–118 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070809 |access-date=November 3, 2018 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On February 10, 2019, he scored a career-high 37 points and made eight 3-pointers in a 120–118 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 10, 2019 |title=Cousins' late free throws lead Warriors past Heat 120–118 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071511 |access-date=February 10, 2019 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> He missed games at the end of the season with heel and groin injuries.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2019 |title=Sources: Heat's Richardson could miss 2 weeks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26439534/sources-heat-richardson-miss-2-weeks |access-date=April 6, 2019 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> Richardson's per-game averages of 16.6 points and 4.1 assists were the highest of his NBA career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hudrick |first=Paul |date=October 3, 2019 |title=Don't forget about Josh Richardson, 'the secret' for Sixers' starting 5 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/josh-richardson-sixers-heat-starting-five-brett-brown-jimmy-butler |access-date=October 8, 2019 |website=NBC Sports Philadelphia}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2019–2020)===
On July 6, 2019, Miami traded Richardson to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] as part of a package for [[Jimmy Butler]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2019 |title=HEAT Acquire Butler And Leonard |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-butler-leonard-190706 |access-date=July 6, 2019 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> On December 12, Richardson scored 14 points in a 115–109 win against the [[Boston Celtics]]. Coach [[Brett Brown]] called him a "dot connector" and "bridge builder".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Carlin |first=Ky |date=December 13, 2019 |title=Brett Brown says Sixers would have 'struggled' without Josh Richardson |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/13/brett-brown-says-sixers-would-have-struggled-without-josh-richardson/ |access-date=December 16, 2019 |work=Sixers Wire}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2020–2021)===
[[File:Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Dallas Mavericks (51176484408) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Richardson takes a [[layup]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] during a game against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2021]]
On November 18, 2020, Richardson, along with the draft rights to [[Tyler Bey]], were traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Seth Curry]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |date=November 18, 2020 |title=Mavericks acquire Josh Richardson, but are 'not done yet', Nelson says |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-trade-rumor/ |access-date=November 19, 2020 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> His season was characterized by [[Sports Illustrated]] as "disappointing" as Richardson's production dropped significantly in the playoffs. In 7 games against the Los Angeles Clippers, he scored only 4.9 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 0.7 assists in 13.4 minutes per game.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Afseth |first=Grant |title=Mavs Trading Josh Richardson To Celtics - And Here's Why |url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavs-trading-josh-richardson-boston-celtics-why-nba-news-kyle-lowry |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2021–2022)===
On July 31, 2021, Richardson was acquired by the [[Boston Celtics]] using the remainder of the [[Gordon Hayward]] traded player exception in exchange for young center [[Moses Brown (basketball)|Moses Brown]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 31, 2021 |title=Celtics Acquire Josh Richardson from Mavericks |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-josh-richardson-mavericks |access-date=July 31, 2021 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Bontemps | first=Tim | title=Sources: C's acquire Richardson, trade Thompson | website=ESPN.com | date=2021-07-30 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31923009/sources-boston-celtics-acquire-josh-richardson-trade-tristan-thompson-separate-3-team-deal | access-date=2025-12-10}}</ref> On August 24, the Celtics announced that they had signed Richardson to a contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Celtics Sign Josh Richardson to Contract Extension |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-josh-richardson-contract-extension |access-date=August 24, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He had a 27-point outing in a win against the New York Knicks.

===San Antonio Spurs (2022–2023)===
On February 10, 2022, Richardson was traded along with [[Romeo Langford]] to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[Derrick White]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 10, 2022 |title=Fifth-year guard joins Boston backcourt; Langford, Richardson, 2022 protected first-round draft pick to San Antonio |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-derrick-white-spurs |access-date=February 10, 2022 |website=nba.com}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Pelicans (2023) ===
On February 9, 2023, Richardson was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Devonte' Graham]] and four future second-round picks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pelicans acquire Josh Richardson |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-josh-richardson-trade-spurs-devonte-graham |access-date=February 9, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref>

=== Return to Miami (2023–2025) ===
On July 2, 2023, Richardson signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAT SIGN JOSH RICHARDSON |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-josh-richardson |access-date=July 2, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref>

On February 6, 2025, Richardson was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in a five-team trade, including [[Jimmy Butler]] to the [[Golden State Warriors]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/jimmy-butler-heading-to-warriors-in-multi-player-deal-with-heat|title=Jimmy Butler joins Warriors in 5-team deal with Heat|date=February 6, 2025|website=nba.com}}</ref> but was waived shortly after.<ref>{{cite web |title=Utah Jazz Waive Josh Richardson |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-josh-richardson |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 10, 2025 |date=February 9, 2025}}</ref>

=== Basket Zaragoza (2026) ===
On January 23, 2026, Richardson signed with [[Basket Zaragoza]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and [[FIBA Europe Cup|Europe Cup]]. Richardson signed a contract until the end of the season with an initial 10-day trial period,<ref>{{cite web |title=Josh Richardson: experiencia NBA al servicio del Casademont Zaragoza |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/544587-josh-richardson-experiencia-nba-al-servicio-del-casademont-zaragoza.html |website=acb.com |access-date=January 23, 2026 |date=January 23, 2026 |language=es}}</ref> ultimately averaging 9.6 across five appearances for the team. On February 27, Richardson and Zaragoza reached an agreement to put an end to his contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Casademont Zaragoza y Josh Richardson separan sus caminos |url=https://www.casademontzaragoza.es/noticias/casademont-zaragoza-y-josh-richardson-separan-sus-caminos |website=casademontzaragoza.es |access-date=February 27, 2026 |date=February 27, 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

On July 30, 2026, Richardson announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{Cite web |last=HoopsHype |date=July 30, 2026 |title=Josh Richardson announces retirement |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/josh-richardson-announces-retirement-081059516.html |access-date=July 30, 2026 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>
